correctness.rationale: The lexicographic order of padded triples has at most three later-neighbor transfer types. When c>0 the specific neighbor (a+1,b,c-1) is adjacent to each later neighbor; for c=0 the only later neighbor is (a+1,b-1,0). Thus every sequential deletion is a closed-neighborhood domination, yielding an all-n strong collapse. At n=8 with at most four parts, nine fixed graph folds leave K6 minus a perfect matching, whose flag complex is the join of three S0, hence S2 over the integers. Independent row-transfer and conjugate-coordinate graph generators agree in tested cases. The exact verifier independently checks the finite neighbor inclusions, independent adjacency comparisons and octahedral certificate; finite checks do not prove the all-n statement.

value.rationale: The canonical number-of-parts filtration is a natural way to measure complexity in partition spaces. Uniform strong collapsibility gives an explicit all-size topological reduction stronger than homology vanishing, and the first four-part octahedral obstruction demonstrates a sharp filtration boundary at the size where the unrestricted topology first becomes nontrivial. This is neither a new tabulated scalar nor a special case of the unrestricted wedge rank.
